answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% spend cut, the low-cost vendor's quote alone meets that mandate, and the primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew. memory_c2 documents that moving primary supply to the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply, onboarding was quick, and invoicing stayed accurate—directly relevant precedent for this switch. memory_c6 documents that multi-year incumbent commitments unlocked volume pricing without narrowing service scope, which suggests a possible negotiation lever if we instead renewed and pressed for terms, but that path likely does not reach the 18% mandate on its own. Note on delivery risk: the line runs at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, so I am flagging downsream value risk—if the low-cost vendor stumbles even briefly, the line has no cushion. I am preserving that uncertainty in the decision and would recommend a same-day onboarding and a short overlap window to protect throughput before fully transferring volume.
